title: Hiromasa Okujima Announces 1st Original Boys-Love Manga
content:
Hiromasa Okujima announced on X (formerly Twitter ) on Wednesday a new "yankee" boys-love manga that will launch with Manga Box 's new Comic Fetto label in 2027, with a possible release window in summer. According to the artist, this marks his first original boys-love manga.

Okujima cited interest in writing a title in the genre after he finishes the Baban Baban Ban Vampire manga, which has elements of boys-love .

Okujima announced on October 31 the Shijūkara ga Naku Koro ni (When The Japanese Tit Sings) manga will end in the eighth chapter. Okujima launched the series on Fusosha 's Manga Spa! platform in December 2025.

Okujima launched the Together with Serial-san ( Serial-san to Issho ) manga in Shueisha 's Grand Jump Mucha magazine on February 25. Shueisha 's new global digital manga platform MANGA MILLION is releasing the manga in English.

Okujima launched the Baban Baban Ban Vampire manga in Akita Shoten 's Bessatsu Shōnen Champion magazine in October 2021. Akita Shoten published the manga's 14th compiled book volume on August 6. The manga is entering its "final stage" in the 15th volume on December 8. The series inspired an anime that streamed on Netflix in January 2025, along with a live-action film that opened in July 2025. Dark Horse licensed the manga for English release, and released the first volume on November 10.

Viz Media 's SuBLime imprint for boys-love manga licensed SHOOWA and Okujima's Bad Boys, Happy Home ( Dōsei Yankee Akamatsu Seven ) manga, and released the first volume physically and digitally in July 2021. The pair launched the manga in Akita Shoten 's Kachi Comi magazine in April 2018.

Okujima's Katei Kyōshi no Kishi Knight Desu. (I Am the Home Tutor Kishi Knight.) manga inspired a live-action series adaptation that premiered on January 5. Okujima serialized the manga in Akita Shoten 's Nicchan Gecchan magazine in 2019. Akita Shoten published one volume for the manga.

title: 5 1990s Anime Classics That Still Hit Today
content:
When it comes to anime classics, t he 1990s was a different era altogether . It was the most revolutionary time for the anime industry since the medium broke into the global mainstream. The anime industry saw a massive change in the animation style with the exceptional hand-drawn cel animation and detailed layouts, before animation studios shifted to digital ink and paint toward the late 1990s. While TV broadcasts were mostly shows suitable for kids, the mainstream anime medium shifted towards darker and more intense storytelling. This was a breakthrough for the anime industry as it became mainstream through older fans.

While the 2020s keep seeing an oversaturation of shows and movies, the 1990s released fewer but iconic anime , most of which are loved even to this day. Anime created during that era were a lot more experimental since they allowed directors and animators more artistic freedom. This is evidenced by the fact that many classics fans love today are still unmatched in terms of both storytelling and animation style. If you haven’t already watched these 1990s anime classics, then now is the perfect time to do so.

5) Yu Yu Hakusho

Yoshihiro Togashi isn’t just known for Hunter x Hunter , but he actually made a name for himself in the industry through the Shonen Jump hit, Yu Yu Hakusho . There’s no denying that the anime suffered from poor pacing and animation inconsistencies. However, what really matters is that it remains entertaining despite the issues while also having a unique premise that hasn’t been replicated even today. The anime began airing decades ago, and even now, not many series can keep viewers hooked as it did.

While the animation isn’t flashy, it stands out for its impeccable fight choreography, something Studio Pierrot was unmatched in during the 1990s and 2000s. A huge reason behind the success of this anime is that it killed off its protagonist at the beginning of the story, after which the story took one unexpected turn after another. Whether it’s the character development or the world-building, Togashi proved why he is known as one of the greatest creators of all time.

4) Perfect Blue

Directed by the legendary Satoshi Kon, the film hit the Japanese theaters in 1998 and eventually became one of the greatest psychological thrillers of all time, not just in anime but in all mainstream media. This psychological horror film stands out for blurring the line between reality and fantasy, all the while depicting some of the best visuals seen in the industry. The film’s animation and visual storytelling have never been recreated with modern animation, making it all the more distinctive and memorable.

Not to mention that this film earned Satoshi Kon worldwide recognition, kickstarting his legendary career. The story centers around Mima Kirigoe, who leaves her famous J-pop idol group to pursue her acting career, but before long she gets entangled in a series of strange events that make her question her own sanity. The movie masterfully blends mind-bending storytelling while focusing on the gradual deterioration of Mima’s mental state as she is unable to tell reality from delusion apart.

3) Princess Mononoke

Princess Mononoke is pretty much an obvious entry to this list of 1990s anime classics. If you have been an anime fan for quite a while, there’s no way you haven’t watched any films by Studio Ghibli. The studio’s trademark is hand-drawn animation with exceptional attention to detail, including lush landscapes, fluid movement, and expressive characters featuring visually stunning scenes. Among the many classics from the studio, Princess Mononoke stands out for its darker tone, as it focuses on the moral ambiguity of the main characters.

While Ghibli is known for its whimsical fantasies, this classic depicted intense battle violence all the while portraying the reality of human conflict. Many fans don’t even know, but this movie basically saved Ghibli from bankruptcy. It was released during the time when Ghibli was dealing with financial strain , and probably would have had to close down if it flopped. Luckily, Princess Mononoke became a massive hit after its premiere, and it’s loved among fans even now.

2) Ghost in the Shell

While the anime remake by Science SARU is one of the best anime series of the year, the legacy of the original film is impossible to beat. Directed by the legendary Mamoru Oshii, the Ghost in the Shell film is a pioneer of new animation techniques, known for its stunning visuals through the use of a blend of traditional cel animation with early computer-generated imagery. The movie isn’t a faithful adaptation of the manga by Masamune Shirow, unlike the 2026 reboot, but it has its own charms. The movie took a much darker tone than the original manga, especially with the protagonist Motoko Kusanagi.

While she appeared much more cheerful in the manga, her personality in the movie suited the intense themes in the movie, especially considering its futuristic setting. Set in the year 2029, Major Motoko Kusanagi, a cyborg agent in Japan’s elite Public Security Section 9, is tasked with tracking down a mysterious hacker who hijacks cyborg brains through the internet. However, she never would have imagined that her search for the hacker would bring her closer to the truth behind the cyborg world, which blurs the lines between humans and machines.

1) Cowboy Bebop

If we’re talking about timeless 1990s classics, we can’t leave out this masterpiece by director Shinichirō Watanabe. Thanks to its space western themes, striking visuals, fluid action sequences, and jazz soundtrack, the series stood the test of time and remains one of the most beloved anime even now. The striking visuals are appreciated even more now since it’s virtually impossible to recreate them anymore. Aside from the visuals, Cowboy Bebop is often praised for its flawed characters and the tragic undertones.

Not only that, but the English dub surpassed even the original version , making it even more popular in the West. The story takes place in the year 2071, when humanity has spread across the galaxy, and the increase in crimes is causing an era of unrest. The only people capable of stopping these criminals are space bounty hunters, including those aboard the spaceship Bebop. While the story begins as a space adventure, it takes a drastic turn as it explores the protagonist’s complex past that comes back to haunt him.

Do you agree with our picks – or have an anime in mind that you want to add here? Share your recommendations in the comments below.

title: Duel Masters GT Manga Gets 4th Part
content:
Shogakukan 's Weekly CoroCoro Comic manga website announced on Wednesday that Hiroki Kikuzuma and Daisuke Kawasaki 's Duel Masters GT manga will continue in a new arc.

Duel Masters GT3 -Glitch of the Twin Heart- , the third part of the series, ended on the same day.

The third part launched on Weekly CoroCoro Comic on August 6.

The first part of the manga, Duel Masters GT -Gear of the Twin heart- , launched in August 2025, and ended in October 2025. The second part, Duel Masters GT2 -Gate of the Teleport- , launched in December 2025, and ended on February 26.

The Duel Masters Pure Play's manga, based on the Duel Masters Play's smartphone game, launched on Shogakukan 's Weekly CoroCoro Comic manga service on September 14. Reki Yayoi is drawing the manga. Hirokuni Nojima - the art director, character designer, and story writer for Duel Masters Play's - is credited for the manga's original story and supervision.

Based on the long-running Duel Masters trading card game, Yō Kanebayashi and Shigenobu Matsumoto 's Duel Masters LOST Tsuioku no Suishō ( Duel Masters LOST: Crystal of Remembrance) manga launched in February 2024 and ended in March 2024. Kanebayashi and Matsumoto then launched the Duel Masters LOST ~Gekka no Shinigami~ ( Duel Masters LOST: Reaper of the Moon) manga in August 2024, and ended it in February 2025. Duel Masters LOST ~Bōkyaku no Taiyō~ , the third part of the manga, debuted in September 2025. Duel Masters LOST ~Danzai no Shōnen~ (The Sentencing Boy), the fourth part , debuted on March 26, and ended on July 2. The final chapter revealed the manga will have a fifth part titled "Shitsuraku no Duel," which stated on September 17.

title: Dragon Ball Super Needs to Reveal More of Its Multiverse
content:
The entirety of Dragon Ball Super ‘s 131 episode, two-movie run discussed only a small portion of its multiverse. The anime focused on Universe 7, which is where the Z Fighters are located, and specifically Universes 6 and 11 got extended attention compared to the rest. Universe 6 features essentially a fraternal twin to 7 with its own Saiyans, a Frieza variant and Namekians, while 11 contained some of the most powerful characters in the whole series like Jiren and Top .

All other universes were erased for their defeats, before being restored through Android 17’s wish at the end. Universes 6 and 11 got the most airtime before their eliminations, but the tourney also included Universes 2, 3, 4, 9 and 10. Four universes were also absent from the tournament as they had high enough mortal levels to gain an exemption. This means there’s a lot to still unpack. The whole catalogue of Dragon Ball includes 659 episodes of canon and non-canon material, and more than 20 movies, yet that only covered content occurring in one universe . There’s a lot more to dig into.

Universes 6 and 11 Should Get More of a Deep Dive

The most obvious choices to focus more on are Universes 6 and 11, especially 6 . The sister world would give Goku, Vegeta and the Universe 7 Saiyans an opportunity to see what life would’ve been like if their planet wasn’t destroyed. The Saiyans in the alternate world behave much differently. It’s a much more peaceful planet, hence the skinnier, smaller Saiyan fighters. They haven’t needed to battle for their lives numerous times the way Goku and Vegeta have.

This reason alone should open up more possibilities for the future. Goku and Vegeta could go and train Cabba, Caulifla and Kale on how to defend Planet Sadala from an impending threat and keep the Saiyan legacy going. Vegeta already became somewhat of a mentor to Cabba . Ironically, even though Android 17 brought back all the universes, Universe 7’s Planet Vegeta didn’t come back, as it wasn’t going to be erased. So Sadala is the only remaining home world for the Saiyans. An arc surrounding the Z Fighters in Sadala would make for some great material.

Universe 11 boasts an elite unit of fighters named the Pride Troopers, which contain Jiren and Top. The former of which is so powerful that he even outranks the God of Destruction in his world. A character that powerful deserves a longer look just from that fact alone. This group of warriors boasts significant power levels, but also was a unique adversary because the Troopers are morally good individuals. Similar to how Universe 6 contained characters the Z Fighters cared about, it gave the tournament a conflicted vibe. Yes, the audience is rooting for Goku and the Saiyans, but it’s not like they wanted to see the other universes erased either.

Erased Universes And Lesser Worlds Leave More to Explore

The other minor universes don’t get the same amount of devoted time, but they offered up a lot of other races and characters to dive into. The battle with Universe 9 stands out with unique fighting skills from the Trio of Danger. Bergamo, Basil and Lavender give Universe 7 all it can handle, especially Lavender. His poison attack earns him a draw against Gohan, as he blinded the Saiyan and eventually rendered him unconscious. The werewolf race doesn’t go down without a struggle, despite being significantly out of their depth against the Z fighters.

Universe 3 featured one of the better tournament fighters, despite being a lesser world. Anilaza was created through a fusion of four team members, and despite lessening the depth of the roster, the move proved tactically successful. The fused being is stronger than any one individual Z Fighter . It forced the entire team to coordinate their attacks in order to defeat the monster. The fight spans just a couple of episodes, and that’s all fans get in terms of a glimpse into Universe 3. The Tournament of Power is merely a brief description of the rival worlds.

Furthermore, what about the ancient universes (13-18) that were erased? Dragon Ball Super could eventually go into greater detail about how they were destroyed, and why no one ever brought them back with the Dragon Balls. There’s just an endless amount of storylines to tackle beyond the Tournament of Power. Which universe would you like Dragon Ball Super to focus on next? Let us know in the comments.

title: 'You're So Sloppy, Hotta-Sensei' Manga Ends in 2 Chapters
content:
Mao Nakada announced on X (formerly Twitter ) on Wednesday that the You're So Sloppy, Hotta-sensei ( Darashinai Desu Hotta-sensei! ) manga will end in two chapters.

Azuki publishes the series digitally in English, and describes the story:

Makoto Kuribayashi is your typical high schooler with a not-so-typical after-school gig as a housekeeper. His latest client? None other than his school's most popular teacher, the gorgeous Rumiko Hotta. But Hotta-sensei is hiding a dirty little secret: she's a total slob, the polar opposite of her flawless public image! Now, Makoto's got the unenviable task of cleaning up after her mess. Will his admiration for Hotta-sensei survive a dose of harsh reality in this irreverent comedy?

Nakada launched the manga in Futabasha 's Manga Action magazine in March 2022. Futabasha published the manga's 10th compiled book volume on July 9, and will ship the 11th volume on December 10.

title: Demon Slayer Was a Huge Disappointment This Year & It’s Not Because of Infinity Castle
content:
2026 marks the 10th anniversary of the manga debut of Demon Slayer , a Weekly Shonen Jump hit written and illustrated by Koyoharu Gotouge. The series has been on the rise of popular ever since then, but things took a drastic turn after the anime debut by Ufotable in 2019. Fans immediately fell in love with the striking visuals and a lovable protagonist. While the anime is currently in its final stretch, the manga wrapped up its story in 2020 with no hopes of a return with a spin-off or a sequel . Following the conclusion of the Hashira Training Arc in the anime, Ufotable confirmed that the Infinity Castle Arc will be adapted in a trilogy of movies.

The first installment has already been released, while fans await updates on Part 2 . Ever since the anime debuted in 2019, this year is the first time Demon Slayer hasn’t released a new TV season or a movie. Considering the animation quality and the exceptional adaptation, it’s only fair that the studio takes as much time as it needs for another movie. However, the biggest problem wasn’t the lack of a new release for the anime’s continuation but the fact that Demon Slayer didn’t even celebrate its 10th anniversary.

Demon Slayer ‘s 10th Anniversary Was Underwhelming Due to No New Announcements

For a globally popular series like Demon Slayer , the manga’s 10th anniversary is a pretty huge deal. Even if the anime couldn’t return with a new movie this year, fans should’ve gotten new updates for the anniversary or a celebratory message from the creator. This is especially disappointing considering how most series usually make a big deal of the anniversary celebrations. Whether it’s new visuals, merchandise, or even anime or manga projects, fans often get all kinds of new updates to commemorate major milestones. 2026 is almost over, and the anniversary during February was pretty dull. There’s still a possibility that the series will drop new information during this year’s Jump Festa .

Along with a majority of the Shonen Jump hits, Demon Slayer is expected to drop new information during the convention. It will hold a panel on the Super Stage, along with some of the biggest hits of all time, including One Piece and Naruto . title: Online Retailer CDJapan Confirms Potential Customer Information Leaks Caused by Unauthorized Access
content:
Between November 6 at 9:06 p.m. and November 13 at 7:52 p.m. JST, the company noted that a third party had tampered with the credit card information entry page, and there were scripts designed to steal information. CDJapan confirmed that all unauthorized external access routes have since been blocked, and that all detected malicious scripts, malware, and codes have been removed. CDJapan listed that there were 1,152 cases in which customers saw a credit card information entry page with malicious code when ordering items from a computer. In 490 of these cases, there was an action for customers to submit credit card information after seeing the affected page. Credit card information that may have been leaked as a result include credit card numbers, expiration dates, cardholder names, and security codes. The company added that this did not occur for orders placed from smartphones or other devices.

In addition, between 1:04 p.m.-2:15 p.m. JST on November 6, there was a single data extraction of credit card and "certain customer membership information" from its database. Affected information includes 360,538 historical credit card information records for cards registered or used between 2005-2018 and 791,111 members' customer membership information associated with credit card registration. The leaked information includes personal information such as names, email addresses, phone numbers, and partial addresses. The leak also included credit card information, again between 2005-2018, such as numbers, expiration dates, and cardholder names. However, all of these cards have expired already, and the security codes were not included. CDJapan added that there has been no secondary damage so far, such as unauthorized use of credit cards, following this incident.

CDJapan reported the incidents to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission on November 13, the same day that it announced the leak. It is also submitting reports to overseas data protection authorities, requesting enhanced monitoring from credit card companies for unauthorized card number use, contacting customers that were affected by the unauthorized access, fixing identified vulnerabilities, strengthening its security monitoring, and permanently deleting all historical credit card information between 2005-2018 following the investigation's completion.

The company is warning customers to check their credit card statements for any suspicious transactions, watch out for phishing emails and suspicious communications, and review their passwords, especially if the same password is used for CDJapan. CDJapan did state, however, that it has not confirmed password leakage connected to these incidents.

CDJapan will continue to fulfill and deliver all orders during this time.

title: Avatar: Seven Havens Isn’t Seen as a “Kids Show,” Producers Explain
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens might be approachable for younger audiences and fans of all ages, but those behind the series don’t really see it as just a show for kids. Avatar: The Last Airbender originally kicked off the franchise with Nickelodeon decades ago, and with it introduced animation fans to a whole new kind of world through its run. Then it was taken in an even darker direction with releases like The Legend of Korra and Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender in the years since . For Avatar: Seven Havens , it kind of sits in the middle.

Avatar: Seven Havens might star a very young set of twin Avatars for this new era of the franchise, and it might be designed in a different way than The Legend of Korra , but it takes on some intense subject matter that’s especially seen withe final episodes of the debut season. As executive producer Sehaj Sethi explained in a Reddit AMA for the series, the team always intended to make it “accessible to a younger audience, but also be very interesting to older viewers.”

Avatar: Seven Havens Producer Talks the Show’s Darker Themes

“Personally, I think this show really isn’t a kids show,” Sethi stated when asked about whether or not Avatar: Seven Havens was intended for audiences around Pavi and Nisha’s age of 10-11. “The themes we cover are quite dark and mature. We always intended for this show to technically be accessible to a younger audience, but also be very interesting to older viewers .” Elaborating on this further, Sethi explained that they’re not holding back on putting Pavi and Nisha through the wringer, “Even though Nisha and Pavi are children, we don’t hold back on making them face truly traumatic experiences.”

Series producer Ethan Spaulding teased that Avatar: Seven Havens is going to get darker from here on out as well, “[T]he show definitely gets darker as the story progresses,” but played coy as to whether or not it has a chance of getting as dark as The Legend of Korra did. Either way, this is something that has already been put in place with the final episodes of the first season as it has tackled xenophobia, isolationism, fear as a result of that and more. With Pavi exploring more Havens in the coming season , we’re bound to see more of these intense topics.

What Does This Mean for Avatar: Seven Havens’ Future?

Avatar: Seven Havens has been in development for the past few years before the first season finally premiered, and speaking to ComicBook, stars Aishu Devan (Nisha) and Saheli Khan (Pavi) revealed that they had been working on the show since they were 10-11 years old themselves. Noting that production on the third and fourth season had already begun, all they could tease was that there would be plenty of “character development” for the twins moving forward. So it seems like Pavi and Nisha are going to age alongside all of the events in the series.

It won’t be too much longer before we see what’s next as Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2 is already scheduled to kick off its run with Paramount+ beginning on May 21st next year. The new season will be 13 episodes long, and then followed by 13 more episodes with Season 3 releasing later in 2027. The series will then come to an end with Season 4 some time after, so how do you feel about Avatar: Seven Havens right now? Is it a kids show? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

title: Singer/Songwriter Hiromi Ōta Dies at 71
content:
There was a funeral service for close family.

Ōta was born on January 20, 1955 in Tokyo and grew up in Kasukabe, Saitama Prefecture. She made her career debut with the song "Amadare" (Raindrops) in 1974.

She was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2019. She was hospitalized for treatment in 2024.

Ōta performed the theme song for the Chocobo Racing game in 1999. Ōta also voiced Belle in the Japanese version of The Stingiest Man in Town animated U.S. special.

title: One Piece’s New Movie Could Change the Anime Forever
content:
One Piece has been airing for more than 25 years, and over its long run, it has become a part of many fans’ lives. However, it could change forever with a new One Piece movie releasing next year. What One Piece became known for was being the longest-running shonen anime, releasing new episodes every Sunday since 1999, with a few breaks here and there. However, that long-running legacy came to an end when, in 2025, it was announced that starting in 2026, the anime would embrace a 26-episode-per-year format, releasing in only two seasons. This brought an end to the legacy the anime had built over 26 years.

This year, fans got their first look at how this new anime format affected the series, and it is evident that the change will keep the anime on air for a longer time, as the pacing remains largely the same as it was under the old format. However, this year also brought new announcements from Toei Animation, revealing that the studio is working on two movies. One of them, One Piece Film: God Valley , is scheduled to release next year and will adapt events from the original source material, something the series has never done before. This signals a change that could transform the One Piece anime forever.

One Piece ‘s New Movie Release Strategy Could Be Devastating for International Fans

Up until now, every One Piece movie produced has featured an original story, something fans could easily skip since it was never aligned with the main storyline. This meant that if an anime movie failed to receive a theatrical release in certain regions for various reasons, it wasn’t a problem. One of the main factors with anime movies is that they first release in Japan, while international fans have to wait at least a couple of months, if not longer, to watch them. This wouldn’t normally be a problem, but with the new One Piece movie being canon and adapting a major narrative, it could be devastating for international fans who want to experience the movie as soon as it releases. This will certainly be a problem for major Western countries, as seen with Demon Slayer .

Even though Demon Slayer is a huge franchise, especially in the movie format, its latest movie took two months to receive an international release. Considering the upcoming One Piece movie will be a theatrical exclusive for some time, potentially for at least six months, fans who miss it in theaters for whatever reason could face a long wait before it becomes available on streaming platforms. Unlike anime episodes, which release weekly, this could create a significant delay. This essentially means that it could take even longer for One Piece to actually come to an end, something that some fans who want the franchise to last longer may consider a blessing in disguise.

Another impact One Piece ‘s new movie could have on the anime is that, if it becomes a huge success, which is certainly possible given its potential, newer arcs of the series could also be adapted into movies rather than episodes. This could follow the recent trend of popular franchises receiving theatrical anime releases, such as Haikyuu and Demon Slayer , particularly for their finales. Only time will tell how the final arc of the anime will be presented to fans, but it is clear that the wait for the franchise to end has already been extended. In many ways, the One Piece anime has already changed forever.

The One Piece Anime Has Officially Changed Forever

When it was announced that the anime would be following a 26-episode-per-year format , it became clear that the old One Piece anime had already come to an end, with a new, modern format being introduced to the franchise. With the new canon adaptation in movie form, the modernization of the anime franchise has become even more evident. Moreover, One Piece has already embraced the modern anime format more than most other series, all thanks to Netflix’s ambitious project: a reboot of the anime. Netflix will release seven episodes adapting the first arc of the series, with all episodes dropping simultaneously.

This will serve as an entry point for new fans of the series going forward, offering a modernized way to experience the story without having to watch Toei Animation’s adaptation, which consists of over 1,000 episodes. This could also encourage Toei Animation to change its strategy for the anime adaptation, potentially fully embracing the movie format for future arcs, with faster pacing and theatrical releases on the big screen. All these elements point toward the anime industry changing forever, and One Piece ‘s new movie format could mean longer waits for international fans to watch canon events, unless the franchise plans simultaneous international releases, a possibility that unfortunately seems unlikely.
